shower.thought: We're all living in our own movie, but we're convinced everyone else is just an extra.
Time moves differently depending on whether you're waiting for something or dreading it. Maybe time isn't real—maybe it's just emotion pretending to be linear.
You can't remember most of your life, so you're not actually living it. You're living the version your brain decides to keep.
The worst lies are the ones we tell ourselves while fully knowing they're lies.
Death might be terrifying not because it ends life, but because it proves nothing you do will last.
We spend money to buy time, but we waste the time we bought on worrying about money.
If you've ever laughed at a joke you didn't understand, you've experienced what it's like to be someone else for a second.
The only time you actually know how someone sees you is when they stop trying to make you feel good.
We call it "falling" in love, but the terrifying part isn't the fall—it's that you can't control where you land.
Every scar tells a story you've probably already rewritten in your head.
You're not afraid of being alone; you're afraid of finding out who you are when nobody's watching.
The people who say they don't care what others think are usually the ones who care the most—just about different people.
We treat our bodies like they're borrowed, but we act like they'll never be collected.
Forgetting someone is harder than losing them, because losing someone means they mattered. Forgetting means they didn't.
The reason we hate waiting is because it forces us to exist without distraction—and that's what we're really afraid of.
You've never had an original thought, only original combinations of things you've absorbed. Maybe that's all creativity ever was.
The most honest thing people do is what they do when they think nobody's keeping score.
We fear the unknown future while constantly forgetting that everything once was unknown and we survived it anyway.
Bravery isn't the absence of fear; it's continuing when fear is the loudest voice in the room and you listen anyway.
If you can't remember the last time you did something for the first time, maybe you've stopped living and started existing.

darkjoke.thought: I told my friend his marriage was on the rocks. He said, "At least it's going somewhere."
My therapist asked if I ever thought about suicide. I said, "Only on days ending in Y."
I joined a support group for pessimists. Turns out we were all just waiting for it to fail.
My dad said, "Son, I'm proud of you." I said, "Thanks for the vote of confidence." He said, "I didn't vote for you either."
I have a stepladder because my real ladder left when I was just a kid.
The doctor told me I had six months to live. I couldn't pay the bill, so he gave me another six months.
My wife said I was emotionally unavailable. I said, "That's not true, I'm available every other Thursday."
I used to play Russian roulette. Now I just use LinkedIn.
My friend said he was going through a existential crisis. I said, "Welcome to my permanent state."
The worst part about time travel is knowing what you're going to regret.
I told my counselor I couldn't stop thinking about my ex. She said that's normal. I said, "Even in the shower?" She said, "How long have you been in there?"
My wife asked me to be more spontaneous. So I left.
The doctor said I needed to cut back on drinking. So now I drink in smaller glasses.
I asked my boss if I was getting a raise. He laughed for ten minutes. Still waiting for the punchline.
My therapist says I'm self-destructive. I said, "You're just figuring this out?" She said, "No, I'm still working on the reason why."
I told my friend I was thinking about becoming a minimalist. He said, "You already are—you minimize your effort at everything."
I said goodbye to my childhood today. It said, "Finally."
My girlfriend said I never listen to her. At least I think that's what she said.
Dating in your thirties is like shopping at a clearance sale—everything's marked down for a reason.
I started a business helping people with social anxiety. No one showed up to the grand opening. Best day ever.
